chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd Allah ibn Muskān from Abū Basīr who said:
I asked Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) about a man who stipulates in his Hajj that if he is prevented, he is exempt; is the Hajj obligatory upon him for the following year? He said: Yes.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Hajj if a pilgrim stipulates exemption due to being prevented?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the legal mechanism of 'shart al-tahallul' (stipulating release), where a pilgrim pre-emptively conditions their exemption from Hajj if prevented by an obstacle. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that this condition is valid, meaning the obligation is suspended for the current year but remains binding for the subsequent year, reflecting the principle that the duty is not extinguished but deferred. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that Hajj is a recurring obligation tied to one's ability, rather than a one-time event that vanishes upon a single missed opportunity due to valid impediments.
